carousel.title: 1. Overview
carousel.heading: A six-week campaign that broke APS enrollment records
carousel.content:
inspirED Summer: Academic Recovery Academy Campaign
Atlanta, GA - Atlanta Public Schools - 2021

We designed and executed a district-wide enrollment campaign from scratch in six weeks - brand, app, paid media, direct outreach, earned press, and a live concert series - for Atlanta Public Schools' Summer Academic Recovery Academy. The district's previous best summer enrollment was approximately 5,600 students. They needed families who had spent a year disengaging from school to choose to come back. We enrolled 12,800 - a historic district record, 128% above any prior year.

carousel.title: 2. Details
carousel.heading: $1.275M full-service campaign for APS Office of Academics
carousel.content:
- Client: Atlanta Public Schools (APS) - Office of Academics
- Engagement type: Full-service campaign design, management, and execution
- Contract value: $1,275,000
- Timeline: April-July 2021 (six weeks from contract to launch)
- Student target: Up to 20,000 enrolled in the Summer Academic Recovery Academy (ARA), grades PK-12
- Channels managed: Paid social, Google PPC, programmatic display, radio, direct mail, door-to-door canvassing, SMS, call center, earned media, custom web application
- Partner ecosystem: 4 primary partners coordinated (inspirED Summer, Inc.; Pros 4 Education; The Ludacris Foundation; The Black Gents Foundation)

carousel.title: 3. The Situation
carousel.heading: Academic recovery after a year of pandemic disengagement
carousel.content:
Atlanta's students entered the summer of 2021 carrying one of the heaviest burdens of the pandemic. Black, Hispanic, and low-income students had lost disproportionately more instructional time - researchers estimated students of color stood to lose 11 to 12 months of learning if nothing changed. Pandemic fatigue was not a metaphor. Families were exhausted, distrustful, and disengaged from institutions that had asked a great deal of them during a year of remote learning with uneven support.

APS moved to address the crisis directly, launching the Summer Academic Recovery Academy - a full-day, district-wide program combining academic recovery with social-emotional support for students in grades PK-12. The enrollment goal was audacious: up to 20,000 students, more than triple the district's all-time best of approximately 5,600. The program was real. The urgency was real. The problem was that no family was going to show up simply because the district asked them to.

The campaign needed to be designed for people who had every reason not to participate - and launched in April, with summer starting in June.

carousel.title: 4. The Ask
carousel.heading: Solve a trust and motivation problem in disguise
carousel.content:
APS engaged us to solve an enrollment problem that was really a trust and motivation problem in disguise.

What the work actually required:

- A brand built from zero - no existing campaign identity, no visual language, no tone of voice for what this program was or why it was different from the summer school families already associated with failure
- A WIIFM proposition strong enough to move a disengaged population - not informational outreach, but a genuine behavioral incentive architecture
- Multi-channel campaign management at district scale - reaching families across a major urban school district through paid, earned, owned, and direct channels simultaneously
- A technology layer to track and sustain engagement - registration alone wasn't enough; students needed a reason to show up every day once they enrolled
- Celebrity and partner coordination - managing public-facing ambassador relationships, PR activity, and a live concert series as the campaign's anchor incentive
- A six-week production timeline - from signed contract to full campaign launch, with no existing infrastructure to build on

carousel.title: 5. The Approach
carousel.heading: Treat it as motivation, not communications
carousel.content:
We made one diagnostic decision early that shaped everything else: this was not a communications problem. It was a motivation problem. APS could send every email, post every flyer, and make every robocall - and still fall short - because none of those tactics gave a student a reason to want to go to summer school. The campaign needed to reframe what summer school was before it could persuade anyone to attend it.

We built the strategy around a single principle: meet families where their attention and their values already lived. For the student audience, that was pop culture, peer recognition, and the prospect of access - concerts, prizes, experiences - not brochures about learning recovery. For parents, it was the credibility signal of seeing trusted community figures endorse the program. For teachers, it was acknowledgment of a year that had pushed them to the edge. Every channel, every creative decision, and every outreach activity was designed to carry one of those specific messages to one of those specific audiences.

The operational architecture followed from the strategy. No single channel would reach 20,000 families, so we built a layered outreach stack - paid digital, radio, print, door-to-door, SMS, and call center - sequenced so each wave reinforced the one before it. The custom engagement application was not an add-on; it was the spine of sustained participation once students enrolled, converting a one-time registration into a daily behavioral loop tied to rewards.

carousel.title: 6. The Work
carousel.heading: Brand, app, media, outreach, earned press, and internal rollout
carousel.content:
Brand identity - built from scratch
We developed the complete inspirED Summer brand system: a logo suite with seven variations, a full color palette with CMYK, RGB, HEX, and PMS specs for print and digital use, a typography system, and a custom icon set. All assets were delivered to APS for permanent ownership and future use.

Custom engagement application - designed, built, and deployed
We ran user journey and wireframe workshops with the inspirED Summer team, then designed, developed, tested, and deployed the inspirED Summer Rewards Web Application - a gamified platform where students and parents completed tasks, took surveys, and checked into events to earn points toward prizes and concert access. The app soft-launched May 15, 2021, reached 700+ registered users in 14 days, and averaged 2+ engagement activities per user immediately after registration.

Paid media campaign - three platforms, three phases
We managed a phased paid advertising campaign across Facebook/Instagram (custom audience targeting via parent contact lists, 60-65% match rate), Google PPC (search terms segmented by grade level and school type), and programmatic display (placements on ESPN, CNN, and comparable high-traffic inventory). Total results: 1,004 conversions, 2,686,253 impressions, 32,944 clicks, $41.83 cost per acquisition.

Direct outreach operations
We deployed door-to-door canvassers with 10,000 door hangers and 8,000 postcards across Atlanta neighborhoods. Our call center ran 3 contact attempts per household at 2,000 calls per day, achieving 13,406 connected calls. A six-step SMS countdown sequence - timed to the May 15 registration deadline - reached 25,856 contacts.

Content and earned media
We produced 62 days of daily social media content across May and June 2021, including sequenced countdown posts, sponsor recognition, winner announcements, and educator appreciation content, anchored by 8 campaign hashtags. The earned media campaign generated 92 press placements reaching a combined potential audience of 147 million, including V-103, Yahoo Finance, MarketWatch, AP News, and Rolling Out.

Internal communications infrastructure
We built and delivered a full APS internal rollout kit: email templates for parents and staff, text message scripts, social media caption guidance, print-ready flyers and postcards, robo-call scripts, and class announcement language - enabling the district's own network to amplify the campaign without requiring additional production time.

carousel.title: 7. The Impact
carousel.heading: 12,800 students enrolled and 92 press placements secured
carousel.content:
The campaign produced the highest summer school enrollment in Atlanta Public Schools history.

- 12,800 students enrolled in the Summer Academic Recovery Academy - a historic district record
- 128% above APS's previous all-time best of approximately 5,600 students
- 300% increase in attendance and engagement across the program
- 2,000,000+ total campaign impressions across all channels
- $110,000 in gifts and prizes distributed to participating students, teachers, and families
- 600+ staff served through the campaign's educator engagement and recognition programming
- 1,928 form submissions captured through the campaign website (32,853 total site views)
- 92 press placements with a combined potential audience of 147,000,000
- 700+ app users acquired within 14 days of the platform's full launch

carousel.title: 8. The Deliverables
carousel.heading: A full campaign operating system
carousel.content:
Campaign proposal and fee structure - A scoped, milestone-based contract with phased payment tied to weekly deliverables, submitted to APS Office of Academics.

inspirED Summer brand system - Complete identity package including 7 logo variations, primary and accent color palettes (CMYK/RGB/HEX/PMS), typography system, and custom iconography; delivered to APS for permanent ownership.

inspirED Summer Rewards Web Application - Custom-built gamification platform enabling task completion, survey responses, and event check-ins for points redeemable toward prizes and concert access; includes user journey maps and wireframes from design workshops.

Campaign website - Developed, tested, and deployed lead capture and information site; generated 32,853 views and 1,928 form submissions over the campaign period.

Paid advertising campaign (three phases) - Facebook/Instagram, Google PPC, and programmatic display; 1,004 total conversions at $41.83 CPA across 2,686,253 impressions.

Social media content calendars - May and June 2021 - 62 days of daily posts with sequenced copy, creative direction, and 8 campaign hashtags across all platforms.

Direct outreach operations - Call center (13,406 connected calls), SMS countdown sequence (25,856 texts), door-to-door canvassing (10,000 door hangers, 8,000 postcards).

Earned media campaign - Press release, ambassador coordination, and PR outreach resulting in 92 placements and a 147M potential audience including V-103, AP News, and Rolling Out.

APS internal communications toolkit - Templated email copy (parent and staff versions), text message scripts, social media caption guidance, print-ready flyers and postcards, robo-call scripts, and class announcement language for district-wide internal amplification.

Managed IT infrastructure - Installation and management of Slack, CRM, project management, and email platforms for an 18-person campaign team over the full engagement period.

Concert series production - Live event coordinated as the campaign's flagship attendance incentive, promoted across all paid and earned channels.
